q8.answer: The MERGE updates a matched row only when stg.updated_at >= tgt.updated_at, so an older re-extracted copy never overwrites a newer one. Staging is first deduplicated to one row per order_id (highest updated_at, ties by later deleted_at, then highest staging row id), and the merge is keyed on order_id.

q9.answer: It is stored in etl.pipeline_state.hwm_updated_at in the warehouse. At commit it is set to GREATEST(current hwm, max updated_at of the batch), unchanged if the batch is empty. This happens inside the same transaction as the MERGE, so it moves only when the data commits.

q10.answer: The load is one warehouse transaction (MERGE, HWM update, succeeded status, then COMMIT). Dashboards read only dw.orders, so they see either the previous state or the whole new night. Staging is never visible to them, and a rollback or dropped connection leaves nothing partial. If the engine cannot put these in one transaction, the fallback is an atomic table swap or view flip. That fallback is a stated assumption, not a chosen engine.

q11.answer: Each attempt gets a new run_id, and its start step deletes staging rows of all earlier run_ids, so the failed attempt's staged data is cleared. The retry re-reads the unchanged HWM and uses the same window, hwm - 2h with no upper bound, from a fresh snapshot.

q12.answer: For each mismatched creation day, it re-reads all replica rows with that created_at date, from the same repeatable-read snapshot used for the comparison, into staging. It applies them with the same guarded merge in one transaction. It does not touch the nightly HWM, because it is a repair path only.
